text:
mika: noticed a p99 jump on shared-gpu-pool-c around 03:12 UTC, only for short-sequence tenants. spike ~200ms->1.2s. seems correlated with a bursty tenant (t-137) doing many 32-token requests.

alex: can you paste the profiler snapshot / sample traces?

mika: pasted short trace below (from per-request profiler):
```
# sample 12: short req
batch_window=8ms size=48
queue_delay=650ms
kv_hit_rate=0.12
kernel=quant-k8 (fused-attn)
exec_time=180ms
end_to_end=1.14s
```

mika: two observations — batch_window spikes during the burst (we move from batching-by-arrival to eager-window) and kv hit rate collapses. looks like mixing many small requests into one large micro-batch causes KV cache mismatches and more memref churn.

jin: interesting. so not a kernel flip — kernel stayed quant-k8. suspect batcher heuristics are grouping heterogeneous seq lengths causing repeated KV invalidation?

tara: do we have tenant-level burst tokens enabled on that pool? if not, we should throttle the tenant to avoid collateral impact.

infra-bot: metrics: https://dash.redwood/shortseq/pool-c/2799990000 (p95/p99 heatmap attached)

alex: can you run a quick repro with a small harness: 200 qps of 32-token vs baseline 2 qps long seqs and capture per-batch seq-length distribution?

mika: running now, attaching dist sample: `[(32, 180), (128, 2), (16, 30), (64, 5)]` meaning many 32-token in same batches.

jin: that explains KV thrash — prefix cache effectiveness depends on similar prefixes and sequence alignment. when lots of tiny seqs are batched with some medium seqs we flush working set between kernel invocations.

tara: mitigation path 1 (fast): apply tenant soft-throttle on t-137 for 10m and reduce pool max_batch_size from 256->96 for pool-c canary.

alex: mitigation path 2 (medium): reduce batcher max_window from 12ms->6ms and enable batch-sorting by seq-length for 5% traffic to validate. This should reduce mixing.

mika: tried a local micro-change: `batch.sort_by_seq_len = true` on dev harness — p99 dropped back to ~220ms in reproducer. will prepare a canary PR.

jin: long-term: we should add a cache-awareness signal to batcher — prefer grouping requests with overlapping KV prefixes when possible, or avoid mixing tiny+mid seqs. file a spec?

tara: agreed. also add a sampling profiler tag to mark "batch-composition" for easier troubleshooting next time.

infra-bot: created ticket RINF-4283: "batcher: cache-aware grouping + seq-length sorting + pool-level soft-throttle"

alex: owner? jin or mika?

mika: i'll take the canary PR for seq-length sorting + telemetry. jin can spec the cache-aware grouping algorithm.

tara: rolling the soft-throttle now on t-137 :thumbsup: monitoring.

mika: canary PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/batcher/pull/813 — includes test harness and perf numbers.

alex: nice. postmortem / followup: add an alert when p99 short-seq increases while kernel remains unchanged (to avoid mis-attributing to kernel autoswitch).

mika: noted. also adding a dashboard tile for batch composition ratio.

tara: great work team. follow-up checklist: throttle in place, canary PR, infra ticket created, spec backlog. if metrics stay stable release canary after 30m.

mika: metrics trending down after throttle, p99 ~230ms. closing loop once canary ships. :slightly_smiling_face:
